title: Implement burst-filtering and gradual escalation for SLO paging
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Follow-up action from the March capacity regression postmortem: reduce noisy pagers by implementing a burst-filtering layer ahead of burn-rate gating, plus a graded escalation ladder that increases response severity only for sustained signals. The goal is to reduce one-off flares and autoscaler-induced oscillation pages while preserving fast escalation for true degradation. This ticket covers design, implementation, testing, and rollout plan for Canary -> Staged -> Global rollout with metrics and rollback criteria.
timeline: 2026-03-05 - Ticket created after postmortem review; assigned to Liam to lead implementation
2026-03-06 - Spike: prototype EWMA-based burst filter that suppresses <30s spikes evaluated against historical incidents
2026-03-08 - Found interaction between autoscaler churn and existing burn hysteresis that caused repeated short-lived pages
2026-03-09 - Design review with Oncall and Reliability: agreed on two-layer approach (burst filter + graded escalation), and safe default thresholds
2026-03-10 - Implementation started: added filter as pre-eval stage in alert pipeline; initial unit tests added
2026-03-11 - Integration test in staging with synthetic traffic; measured reduction of pages for transient spikes by ~72% while maintaining detection of sustained 5m burns
2026-03-12 - Rolling canary plan drafted; oncall playbook updated with new escalation ladder and clear rollback criteria
decisions: Use EWMA (alpha=0.25) with a 60s smoothing window as the default burst filter to attenuate transient token-level spikes
Keep existing burn-rate math unchanged, but add a pre-check that requires the filtered burn to exceed threshold for >= 90s before starting tier-1 alerting

Introduce a three-stage escalation ladder: Tier A (non-pager notification to SRE rotation), Tier B (soft pager to primary oncall), Tier C (hard pager and incident kickoff) — each stage requires progressively longer persistence or higher impact
Allow per-service tuning and opt-outs for high-sensitivity flows (e.g., customer-facing SLAs) via service metadata in the alert pipeline
Fallback behavior: if the burst-filtering service is unreachable, revert to existing behavior (no suppression) to avoid blind spots; add telemetry to monitor filter health
tradeoffs: Increased time-to-page for some real regressions at the margin (up to 90s) in exchange for much lower noise and fewer wake-ups — acceptable per oncall consensus
Added pipeline complexity and a new service to monitor vs. simpler threshold tuning; chose modular filter to avoid coupling with core SLO math
Per-service tuning introduces management overhead; mitigated by sane defaults and a small whitelist for critical services
tests_and_metrics: Synthetic regression scenarios run in staging: measured true-positive detection for sustained 5-minute burns preserved at 98%
Noise reduction KPI: pages/hour for transient spikes reduced by 68-75% across 5 services in staging
Introduce two new SLO dashboard panels: Filter Health (uptime, queue depth) and Alert Latency by Stage
Add telemetry events for every suppression decision to allow offline review and ML-based classification of suppressed events
rollout_plan: Canary (Day 0-3): enable filter for non-critical services in us-west-2; monitor pages and SLO alerts in real-time
Staged (Day 4-10): expand to mid-critical services and add Tier-B gating; run handoff drills with oncall
Global (Day 11+): enable for all services with standard defaults; keep per-service opt-outs available via config
Rollback criteria: >10% increase in missed sustained SLO breaches or >20% rise in customer-facing errors correlated with filter; immediate rollback if filter health <99% over 1h
implementation_notes: Pipeline change implemented as a lightweight Go microservice sitting in front of the existing burn-rate evaluator
Filter exposes a /health and /metrics endpoint; integration with PagerDuty and Console tracing already wired
Configuration stored in central feature-flag service for rapid toggles during rollout
Follow-up ticket will convert suppression telemetry into training data for a classifier (see ENG-25432 dependency)
next_steps: Complete unit and integration tests and add chaos test that simulates autoscaler flapping
Run canary in production on a single non-critical customer group and collect 72h of telemetry
Schedule post-canary review with SRE, Oncall, PM, and Product to confirm defaults or adjust thresholds
Draft runbook amendment and ship console UI change to expose per-service opt-out toggle
Close ticket with a short post-rollout retrospective and candidate follow-ups for ML-based suppression
comments: 2026-03-06 - Liam: Spike shows EWMA reduces common short bursts; still tuning alpha. PR will include a knob for alpha per service.
2026-03-09 - Priya (Oncall lead): Concerned about hiding fast regressions for critical customers; agreed to per-service opt-outs and short persistence for critical flows.
2026-03-10 - Marco (Reliability): We should add statsd counters for suppressed events vs fired events; useful for post-deploy audits.
2026-03-11 - QA: Staging tests passed; observed one false suppression case tied to an upstream latency spike — added guard to treat correlated latency as a multiplier for persistence requirement.
2026-03-12 - Product (Nina): Good tradeoff. Please ensure we communicate change to support and CS with expected pager frequency improvements and new runbook links.
